setupSteps: Check the machine. Look at the placard for the correct grip and seat adjustment; make sure the stack pin or plate horns are free and nothing is under the weight.

Choose the grip. If the machine has several handle positions, pick the neutral (palms facing each other) or angled one if overhand feels pinchy; either is fine for a beginner. A wide pronated grip is also common. Converging handles bring the hands together overhead; fixed handles stay the same distance apart.
Select the load. Put the weight-stack pin in a low plate (about 20-30 percent of what you think you can press, est.) or load small plates evenly. Push the pin all the way in so it cannot slip.

Seat height: set the seat so that, with you sitting tall and your arms lowered, the handles line up at about shoulder level or just above (ACE; PureGym; est.). The handles should not start below the shoulders (you would be pressing from too low and the elbows would drop behind the body) and should not be above the ears at the start. Sources vary between shoulder level and between shoulders and ears; FitPlate beginner choice: handles at about shoulder to upper-chest level at the start (est.).

Back pad: sit all the way back; the whole upper back and the lower back lightly touch the pad, with only a natural curve in the lower back (not a hard arch). If the pad has an angle, a slightly reclined pad is fine; it is not an incline chest press.
Feet: flat on the floor (or on the foot rest if the seat is high), hip-width apart, knees about 90 degrees.

Handle grip: hands around the handles with thumbs wrapped, wrists straight and stacked over the forearms, elbows slightly below the shoulders at the start. Elbows point out and slightly forward, not flared far to the sides.
Start-gate or assist lever: if the machine has a start lever (it moves the handles into the starting position), use it, then remove your foot or hand from the lever before you press.
Brace and breathe. Sit tall, ribs down, shoulders away from the ears, belly gently tight.

steps.title: Sit and set your back
steps.action: Sit all the way back and set your feet.
steps.visualCheck: Side: head over shoulders, ribs not flared. Front: both shoulders level.

steps.title: Take the handles
steps.action: Grip both handles with thumbs wrapped; check hands start at about shoulder level or just above.
steps.feel: Weight on the front of the shoulders.
steps.visualCheck: Front: wrists above the elbows; elbows slightly below shoulders.

steps.title: Set the shoulders down
steps.action: Gently pull the shoulders down and back, away from your ears.
steps.visualCheck: Front: shoulders low, not touching ears.

steps.title: Press up
steps.action: Press the handles up and slightly inward (on a converging machine they follow the path), without lifting your back off the pad.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back stays on the pad. Front: both handles rise evenly.

steps.title: Finish near full extension
steps.action: Straighten the arms until just short of locking the elbows (a soft elbow); full straight arms are allowed if comfortable.
steps.visualCheck: Front: wrists above the shoulders; no shrug up to the ears.

steps.title: Pause briefly
steps.visualCheck: Side: lower back still against the pad.

steps.title: Lower under control
steps.action: Lower the handles back to about shoulder level (engage the lats to control the descent, ACE) without letting the stack drop.
steps.feel: Shoulders and triceps resisting the weight.
steps.visualCheck: Front: handles level and elbows slightly below the shoulders; the plates or stack do not touch between reps (light touch is fine).

steps.title: Finish the set
steps.action: After the last rep, lower the handles slowly to the start and let go.
steps.visualCheck: Both hands off together; stack at rest; then re-adjust or leave.

commonMistakes.title: Arching the lower back and lifting off the pad
commonMistakes.text: Arching the lower back and lifting off the pad. Why: it turns the press into a worse incline chest press and loads the lower back (most common machine error in the sources). Fix: lower the weight, brace the abdominals, keep the back flat on the pad.

commonMistakes.title: Seat too low or too high
commonMistakes.text: Seat too low or too high. Why: too low starts the press with the elbows far behind the body and stresses the shoulder front; too high shortens the range. Fix: set handles at about shoulder to upper-chest level at the start.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging toward the ears
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging toward the ears. Why: shifts work from the shoulders to the upper traps, and a persistent shrug can pinch the neck and shoulder. Fix: shoulders down and back; drop the load if the shoulders keep rising.

commonMistakes.title: Slamming into full lockout
commonMistakes.text: Slamming into full lockout. Why: snaps the elbows and ends the rep with momentum. Fix: stop just short of lockout if you wish (optional); straighten smoothly.

commonMistakes.title: Using momentum or letting the stack drop
commonMistakes.text: Using momentum or letting the stack drop. Why: removes the tension and risks the shoulder. Fix: 1-2 s up, 2-3 s down; lower with control.

commonMistakes.title: Flaring or dropping the elbows far behind the body
commonMistakes.text: Flaring or dropping the elbows far behind the body. Why: strains the shoulder front. Fix: keep the elbows slightly below the shoulders and in line with the handles.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath for the whole rep
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath for the whole rep. Why: raises blood pressure briefly. Fix: breathe out as you press; do not hold through the set.

commonMistakes.title: Going too heavy for the shoulder
commonMistakes.text: Going too heavy for the shoulder. Why: overloads the shoulder joint and tempts the back to arch. Fix: choose a load with 2-3 reps in reserve (RIR).

commonMistakes.title: Wrong pin or half-inserted pin
commonMistakes.text: Wrong pin or half-inserted pin. Why: the pin can slip out and the stack can drop. Fix: push the pin all the way in and give a light tug.

commonMistakes.title: Skipping the machine's adjustment instructions
commonMistakes.text: Skipping the machine's adjustment instructions. Why: handle starts too low, or the arms are mismatched. Fix: read the placard and ask staff the first time.

safetyNotes: Pin and weights: push the weight-stack pin all the way in, check it before pressing; for plate-loaded, load both sides evenly and check the plates are fully on the horns.

Shoulder impingement: the evidence is mixed. A 2012 meta-analysis (Timmons) found less upward rotation of the shoulder blade in people with impingement, while a 2016 meta-analysis (Park) found no difference in subacromial space; no study was found that shows the machine press causes impingement. Practical advice: start the handles at shoulder level (not below), keep elbows slightly forward in the scapular plane if the machine allows it, use a neutral or angled grip if overhand pinches, avoid pressing through pinching or a painful arc (roughly 60-120 degrees of arm raise, an NSCA tactical-S&C excerpt, snippet), and stop with sharp pain. A machine fixes the path, but the path may not fit your shoulder.
Lower back: keep the back on the pad and ribs down; stop if you feel a pinch or pain in the lower back.
Neck: if you feel neck strain, drop the load and keep the shoulders down.
High blood pressure: breathe continuously; stop 2-3 reps short of failure.
Spotter: not needed on a machine; if you cannot finish a rep, lower the handles slowly to the start.

Gym etiquette: wipe the seat and handles; do not leave the pin set at a heavy load; do not sit on a machine between sets for long when others wait; return plates to the rack; do not film other members.
